aliases: Red Wolf DCD Properties data center campus
status_detail: Unified Government/BPU are in pre-development discussions; local reporting says rezoning/master-plan approvals occurred in 2025 but resident litigation and zoning questions remain pending. Proposed 548-550 acre campus near Kansas Speedway split across Parallel Parkway, six roughly 330,000 sq ft buildings.
notes: County civic agenda page verifies the planning-commission special session; Beacon summarizes the three Wyandotte proposals and power demand. Ingram/DCD add developer, building count and timing. End user not public.

status_detail: PowerTransitions announced an option purchase agreement with Unified Government/Kansas City, Kansas for purchase, demolition, abatement and redevelopment of the former Quindaro Power Station into a roughly 200 MW data center campus. Beacon says UG/BPU remain in pre-development and no final signed agreement is in place as of Jan. 28, 2026.
notes: PowerTransitions states Phase 1 would provide 100 MW by mid-2027 and Phase 2 another about 100 MW by mid-2029, with about 1.524 million sq ft gross floor area on 66 acres. The official/civic PDF is the proposed option purchase agreement surfaced from the UG CivicClerk record.

status_detail: Beacon reports Project Linda as one of three UG/BPU pre-development data center proposals in Wyandotte County, estimated at 200 MW; location and other details not yet publicly available, and no final signed agreements with BPU or Unified Government.
notes: Included under wide-net rule because local reporting identifies a named pre-development proposal, but public details are minimal.

status_detail: Proposed multi-building hyperscale data center campus on about 600 acres in Cave City and unincorporated Barren County; Cave City enacted a 12-month moratorium on new data center applications, and local litigation/utility questions remain. Electric cooperatives said no project application had been filed with them as of June 12, 2026.
notes: WBKO reports 10 buildings of about 200,000 sq ft each, roughly 2 million sq ft total, and about 1,200 MW critical capacity at full build-out. Power would use on-site natural gas generation and East Kentucky Power per the draft impact analysis.
